sources.title: Environment Agency annual report and accounts 2025 to 2026
facts: EA corporate performance and measures provide organisational context, not parcel greenhouse-gas measurements.
Corporate targets, inspections and financial reporting must not be promoted to site emissions observations.

sources.title: Environment Agency business plan 2026 to 2027
facts: The plan sets Environment Agency priorities and performance measures for 2026-27.
Plans and targets are future or management evidence, not observed parcel emissions.

sources.title: Environment Agency corporate scorecard 2025 to 2026 quarter 3
facts: The scorecard reports inspections, permit compliance and a net-zero corporate measure.
Inspection counts and compliance metrics do not directly measure greenhouse-gas releases at a cadastral parcel.

sources.title: Environment Agency data on business environmental performance
facts: The collection links regulated-sector performance reports including water companies and agriculture.
A collection page is provenance and navigation evidence, not an independent emissions observation.

sources.title: Water and sewerage companies EPA methodology for 2026 to 2030
facts: The methodology defines how the Environment Agency assesses water and sewerage company environmental performance.
EPA methodology metrics and ratings are regulatory performance evidence, not parcel GHG measurements.

sources.title: EPA methodology chapter 6 reporting for 2026 to 2030 data
facts: The chapter explains annual EPA publication and company data reporting for 2026-30.
Reporting rules and historic metric publication do not establish physical parcel emissions.

sources.title: EPA methodology chapter 8 forward look and future reporting
facts: The chapter describes ongoing EPA development and future reporting expectations.
Forward-looking regulatory requirements are not observed greenhouse-gas data.

sources.title: Water and sewerage companies in England environmental performance report 2024
facts: The report covers environmental performance of nine water and sewerage companies in England.
Company pollution and compliance performance must remain distinct from operational GHG and parcel attribution.

sources.title: Ofwat IN 26/02 expectations for large water company annual performance reporting 2025-26
facts: The notice sets requirements and clarifications for 2025-26 annual performance reports.
Reporting obligations are not themselves measured emissions.

sources.title: Ofwat audit opinion for the Annual Performance Report 2025-26
facts: Ofwat specifies expected auditor opinion wording for 2025-26 APRs.
Audit assurance strengthens reporting governance but is not an emissions measurement result.

sources.title: Ofwat annual performance report framework
facts: Ofwat requires water companies to prepare APRs under regulatory accounting guidelines.
APR frameworks standardise reporting but do not bind company figures to cadastral parcels.

sources.title: Ofwat RAG 3.16 format and disclosures for the annual performance report
facts: RAG 3.16 defines APR format and disclosure requirements.
Disclosure format is reporting metadata, not direct greenhouse-gas observation.

sources.title: Ofwat historical performance dataset aligned with PR24 definitions
facts: Ofwat publishes historical PR24-aligned performance data mostly based on company APR submissions.
Company historical performance data require metric and boundary interpretation before emissions use and are not parcel measurements.

sources.title: Ofwat PR24 outcomes performance commitments changes and corrections
facts: The page records changes and corrections to PR24 performance commitments including operational GHG water and wastewater.
Correction provenance must be preserved so superseded definitions are not silently mixed.

sources.title: Ofwat PR24 operational greenhouse gas emissions performance commitment wastewater
facts: The wastewater performance commitment uses tonnes CO2e and percentage reduction from a 2024-25 baseline.
Company operational wastewater GHG is an organisational performance measure, not a parcel-bound direct observation.

sources.title: Ofwat PR24 operational greenhouse gas emissions performance commitment water
facts: The water performance commitment defines operational GHG reporting and reduction against a baseline.
Water-company operational GHG must not be transferred directly to individual properties or parcels.

sources.title: Ofwat PR24 final determinations models
facts: The model library includes operational GHG performance commitment and risk models.
Targets, incentive models and performance ranges are not physical emissions observations.

sources.title: Ofwat Water Company Performance
facts: Ofwat compares company APR performance and publishes sector reporting and underlying data.
Regulatory performance comparison does not automatically establish facility or parcel emissions.

sources.title: NAEI Greenhouse Gas Emissions Data
facts: NAEI lists the 2026 UK GHG inventory, pivot table and devolved inventory products.
Inventory datasets have national, devolved or source-sector scopes and must not be treated as cadastral parcel observations.

sources.title: NAEI inventory methodology
facts: NAEI compiles emissions from national statistics and industrial data using international inventory guidance.
Modelled inventory estimation is method evidence, not direct measurement for every parcel.

sources.title: NAEI reports catalogue
facts: The reports catalogue exposes current greenhouse-gas inventory and methodology reports.
Catalogue presence provides provenance and versioning, not a new physical emissions observation.

sources.title: UK Greenhouse Gas Inventory 1990 to 2024 annual report
facts: The 2026 National Inventory Document reports UK greenhouse-gas emissions through 2024.
National inventory totals and methods must not be assigned directly to parcels without supported spatial evidence.

sources.title: Greenhouse Gas Inventories for England Scotland Wales and Northern Ireland 1990-2024
facts: The report provides devolved-government GHG inventories consistent with the UK inventory.
Country-level allocations remain aggregates and do not prove parcel-level emissions.

sources.title: UK Informative Inventory Report 1990 to 2024
facts: The IIR documents inventory methods and includes a published correction note for a transport data statement.
Methodology and correction records must be preserved by vintage and are not parcel observations.

sources.title: NAEI Devolved Government Greenhouse Gas Emissions
facts: The page describes by-source and end-user devolved GHG inventories and international aviation and shipping treatment.
By-source and end-user accounting bases must remain distinct and are not parcel-bound measurements.

sources.title: NAEI Greenhouse Gas Inventory Improvement Project 1 Bioenergy Model
facts: The report is an inventory-method improvement project for bioenergy modelling.
A methodology improvement report does not establish observed emissions for a specific bioenergy facility or parcel.

sources.title: DUKES renewable sources of energy chapter 6
facts: DUKES chapter 6 reports renewable energy capacity, generation and commodity balances.
Energy generation and capacity are activity data, not direct greenhouse-gas emissions.

sources.title: Energy Trends UK renewables
facts: Energy Trends reports renewable capacity and generation including landfill gas, sewage gas and anaerobic digestion.
Bioenergy electricity generation does not equal methane leakage or lifecycle GHG emissions.

sources.title: Renewable Energy Planning Data
facts: The collection links renewable planning database extracts including a May 2026 quarterly extract.
Planning status and project capacity do not measure operational greenhouse-gas emissions.

sources.title: UK greenhouse gas emissions statistics 2026 planned methodology changes
facts: The 2026 methodology changes add industrial wastewater emissions and separate biogas from natural gas in the distribution network.
Method changes can revise historical series and must not be mistaken for new direct parcel measurements.

sources.title: Environment Agency standard rules environmental permitting collection
facts: The collection lists current standard rules and risk assessments for anaerobic digestion, sludge and biogas activities.
Permit eligibility and standard rules are regulatory controls, not measured emissions.

sources.title: SR2021 No 10 anaerobic digestion of non-hazardous sludge at a wastewater treatment works
facts: The permit covers large biological sludge treatment and use of resultant biogas at wastewater treatment works.
Permit scope and capacity limits do not quantify actual methane or CO2 emissions.

sources.title: SR2021 No 10 standard rules text
facts: The rules include management, operations, emissions and monitoring requirements.
Monitoring obligations and permitted activities are not themselves emission measurements.

sources.title: SR2021 No 10 generic risk assessment
facts: The risk assessment addresses diffuse methane and ammonia and accidental CO2 release risks.
A risk pathway is not evidence that a release occurred or its measured mass.

sources.title: SR2021 No 6 anaerobic digestion facility installations
facts: The standard rules cover larger anaerobic digestion installations and updated biogas/biomethane treatment conditions.
Permit eligibility and design capacity do not equal observed emissions.

sources.title: SR2021 No 6 standard rules text
facts: The rules include emissions, monitoring, carbon capture and decarbonisation-readiness conditions.
Compliance conditions do not establish the quantity of GHG physically released.

sources.title: SR2021 No 6 generic risk assessment
facts: The generic risk assessment includes diffuse greenhouse-gas risk such as methane.
Risk assessment evidence must not be promoted to observed release or parcel GHG.

sources.title: SR2021 No 7 anaerobic digestion waste recovery operation
facts: The permit covers smaller anaerobic-digestion waste recovery operations with updated biogas conditions.
Throughput and permit scope are activity/regulatory evidence, not measured emissions.

sources.title: SR2021 No 8 on-farm anaerobic digestion installations
facts: The standard rules cover on-farm anaerobic digestion using farm wastes and were updated for biogas treatment and carbon capture.
On-farm permit status does not measure methane or avoided GHG.

sources.title: SR2021 No 8 standard rules text
facts: The rules define management, operations, emissions and monitoring for qualifying on-farm AD installations.
Rules and operating techniques are not actual emissions results.

sources.title: SR2021 No 8 generic risk assessment
facts: The risk assessment addresses methane, ammonia and accidental CO2 risk pathways.
Potential diffuse emissions are not evidence of a measured atmospheric release.

sources.title: SR2021 No 9 on-farm anaerobic digestion waste recovery operation
facts: The permit covers smaller on-farm AD waste recovery operations and updated gas-treatment conditions.
Permit capacity and accepted waste volumes are not physical GHG measurements.

sources.title: SR2021 No 9 generic risk assessment
facts: The risk assessment includes diffuse methane and ammonia risk from on-farm AD.
Risk controls do not prove release quantity or cadastral attribution.

sources.title: Biomethane from waste resource framework
facts: The framework sets conditions for biomethane from organic waste to achieve end-of-waste status.
Product quality and regulatory status do not quantify methane leakage or lifecycle GHG emissions.
